skill.name: azure-enterprise-infra-planner
skill.description: Plan enterprise Azure infrastructure from workload goals, research Azure resource constraints, and generate reviewed Bicep or Terraform for approved deployments.
skill.summary: Turns Azure workload requirements into WAF-aligned infrastructure plans and IaC generation steps.
skill.author: microsoft

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown formatting, relative reference links, Azure service terminology, and project-local .azure planning artifacts. Confirmed risks are the intentional Azure CLI and Terraform command workflows, plus semantic risks from collecting Azure environment insights and deploying to live subscriptions. No prompt injection attempt was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: The skill can collect Azure environment insights that may reveal tenant topology or security posture.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit opt-in for insight collection, show the selected scope, and document that .azure/insights.json must not contain secrets.

remediation.issue: Deployment guidance can modify live Azure resources through Azure CLI or Terraform.
remediation.suggestion: Keep deployment behind explicit risk acknowledgement, require what-if or plan output first, and recommend sandbox subscriptions for first use.

remediation.issue: Generated plans and parameter files may include sensitive architecture details or accidental secret values.
remediation.suggestion: Add guidance to exclude secrets from project-local planning files and use managed identity or secure parameter mechanisms instead.

semantic_findings.description: The workflow can query an existing Azure environment through insights_get and save the resulting environment insights to project-local files. This can expose sensitive topology and configuration metadata if run with broad scope.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The files explicitly describe collecting insights from the user Azure environment and writing them to .azure/insights.json. The workflow asks for scope, but the collected cloud metadata can still be sensitive.

semantic_findings.title: Live Azure Deployment Capability
semantic_findings.description: The workflow includes deployment phases that run Azure CLI or Terraform apply commands against live Azure resources. The skill has user confirmation gates, but the capability can still create, modify, or destroy cloud infrastructure.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The deployment phase labels the action destructive and requires explicit confirmation. The deployment reference includes Terraform apply and post-deployment resource verification steps.

content.value_statement: Complex Azure infrastructure planning can miss dependencies, security gates, and deployment constraints. This skill guides architecture, WAF review, IaC generation, and cautious deployment.
actual_capabilities: Guides a seven-phase Azure infrastructure planning workflow with approval gates.
Creates project-local insight and infrastructure plan artifacts for review.
Researches Azure resource types, naming rules, and pairing constraints from bundled references.
Generates Bicep or Terraform files under an infra directory after approval.
Checks plans against WAF, dependency, naming, and pairing guidance.
Provides Azure CLI and Terraform deployment steps with confirmation requirements.
limitations: Requires human review before generated infrastructure is used in production.
Depends on Azure tools, Microsoft documentation tools, or local reference fallbacks.
Does not manage credentials, quotas, budgets, or subscription permissions.
Deployment commands can affect live resources and must be run with care.

use_cases.title: Design a Landing Zone
use_cases.description: Create a structured plan for networking, identity, monitoring, and security controls before implementation.

use_cases.title: Generate Reviewed IaC
use_cases.description: Turn an approved Azure plan into Bicep or Terraform files with validation steps.

use_cases.title: Check Architecture Constraints
use_cases.description: Review resource choices against WAF guidance, dependencies, naming rules, and Azure pairing constraints.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Basic Workload
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan Azure infrastructure for a small production web app with a database, monitoring, backups, and secure defaults.

prompt_templates.title: Design Hub-Spoke Networking
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a hub-spoke Azure network with shared firewall, private endpoints, DNS, monitoring, and clear dependency reasoning.

prompt_templates.title: Generate Approved Bicep
prompt_templates.prompt: After I approve the infrastructure plan, generate Bicep files for the selected resources and include validation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Production Deployment
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the approved plan, confirm risks, prepare what-if validation, and list the exact operator checks before deployment.

output_examples.input: Plan infrastructure for a regulated analytics workload in two Azure regions.
output: A phased architecture plan with regions, networking, identity, data, monitoring, and disaster recovery choices.
A review section explaining WAF tradeoffs, dependencies, and required user approvals.
A recommendation for Bicep or Terraform generation after plan approval.

output_examples.input: Generate Terraform for the approved Azure plan.
output: Terraform file organization under an infra directory.
Provider, variable, module, output, and backend guidance tied to the approved plan.
Validation and plan commands the operator should run before applying changes.
A checklist covering naming, dependency, SKU, network, and security constraints.
Required fixes before approval and a clear stop point for manual review.

best_practices: Use a sandbox subscription for first runs and review every generated plan before approval.
Keep real secrets out of planning files and use managed identity where possible.
Run dry-run validation before any deployment and capture operator approval.
anti_patterns: Letting the skill deploy from an unreviewed draft plan.
Storing real secrets in .azure planning artifacts or generated parameter files.
Using production subscriptions for experiments or ambiguous architecture requests.

faq.question: Does this skill deploy infrastructure automatically?
faq.answer: It includes deployment guidance, but its workflow requires explicit approval gates before IaC generation and live deployment.

faq.question: Can it generate both Bicep and Terraform?
faq.answer: Yes. It can generate either format after the infrastructure plan is approved and the user chooses a format.

faq.question: Does it replace an Azure architect?
faq.answer: No. It organizes research, planning, and IaC steps, but production plans still need expert review.

faq.question: Where does it store planning artifacts?
faq.answer: It uses project-local .azure files for insights and plans, and an infra directory for generated IaC.

faq.question: Can it inspect an existing Azure environment?
faq.answer: It can use an insights tool when available, so teams should confirm scope and avoid unnecessary tenant access.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
